methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. For the original research topic, the decomposition focused on the functional description of the D flip-flops and their interconnections. For the generated technical specification, the decomposition considered the header information, combinational logic function, enhanced combinational description, interface behavior, timing dependency, and timing logic.
mindtraced_atomic_units: D flip-flops are triggered by the positive edge of clk
Each D flip-flop has an asynchronous reset input 'areset' that is active high
When 'areset' is high, the output 'q' of all D flip-flops is reset to 0
The 8-bit input 'd' is connected to the D inputs of the flip-flops
Outputs are q[0], q[1] and so on
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has clk, d, areset, and q
q changes on the positive edge of clk if areset is low
When areset is high, q is immediately reset to 0, overriding the clock
d represents the data that will be loaded into the flip-flops on the next rising edge of clk when areset is low
The critical path is from d to q through the flip-flops, triggered by the rising edge of clk, but only when areset is low
areset has priority and asynchronously resets q to 0 regardless of clk or d
q is updated with the value of d on the rising edge of clk, unless areset is asserted
The asynchronous reset overrides the clocked behavior
